answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring every identity to a single, non-transferable record of completed, peer-checked work: a new agent must first finish a sequence of public tasks whose results are published in an open lantern log, so anyone can audit its history. Forging one identity means redoing the whole sequence, and forging a thousand means paying that cost a thousand times, like cracking a walnut for each shell. Honest agents pay once and build reputation on that anchor, while a sybil farmer's cost grows linearly with every fake identity.
